findings.title: Recognition is asymmetrically distributed
findings.claim: In 12:58, recognition is distributed asymmetrically: Yusuf identifies the arriving brothers while their brotherhood and entry into his presence do not return recognition to him.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms إِخْوَةُ and دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ establish the relational encounter, while عَرَفَهُمْ carries Yusuf's one-directional identification and مُنكِرُونَ supplies the independent non-recognition that prevents reciprocity.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene becomes a meeting in which the same relation is cognitively available to one side and withheld from the other.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary brotherhood, entry, recognition, and non-recognition of the focus. It adds only the asymmetry supplied by their juxtaposition and does not claim that the brothers lack every kind of knowledge.

epistemic.reason: The channel evidence is trusted and directly anchored in the focus, while the secondary relational synthesis remains a contextual resonance rather than a replacement translation.

findings.title: Arrival as a controlled basin
findings.claim: As a bounded analogy, the brothers' arrival can be seen as a human flow pooled at a provisioning center whose measures and containers govern departure, return, and retention.
findings.mechanism: The focus arrival carrier is contacted by measured provision, a watering channel or share, and repeated containers, creating a material flow image that returns through the focus coming.
findings.reader_payoff: The provisioning center becomes perceptible as a place that gathers movement, measures release, and retains one part of what arrives.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory spatial-material analogy only. It does not replace the ordinary meaning of coming, does not claim literal water imagery in 12:58, and remains attributed to the legacy-unbound HFT trace.

epistemic.reason: The trace has aligned coordinates and independent material triggers, but it explicitly identifies itself as an outlier and supplies no bound reader identity.

findings.title: Non-recognition does not erase procedural astuteness
findings.claim: The brothers' failure to recognize Yusuf does not erase procedural alertness: they can formulate a rule even while remaining blind to the person and plan that make the rule binding.
findings.mechanism: The focus non-recognition and its attributed astuteness facet are contacted by the brothers' stated penalty formula and by the superior stratagem that turns their own procedural reasoning into the mechanism of retention.
findings.reader_payoff: Non-recognition becomes a local blindness about identity rather than a claim that the brothers are generally witless within the encounter.
findings.containment: The ordinary non-recognition remains primary. The astuteness branch is a surprising, exploratory contrast supported by later procedural speech and does not excuse or condemn the brothers.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and pericope coordinates support the contrast, but the outlier is explicitly exploratory and the HFT identity is legacy-unbound.
